record.body:
## Rationale

A committed baseline lets the `types` job block from the first run. CI fails only on errors that are not in the baseline. The phase fixes the 26 errors under `orchestra/`, so the baseline holds only `dashboard/` and `installer/` entries. The gate then catches every new error without a 100-edit cleanup that conflicts with in-flight phases. The user chose this.

## Counter-argument

Fixing every error with no baseline gives a clean end state and nothing to protect. A baseline is easy to regenerate, and an agent can hide new errors by running `--writebaseline`. Baselined errors also tend to stay forever. About 75 edits in `dashboard/` and `installer/` is a bounded cost.

payload.alternatives: fix every error with no baseline
payload.choice: fix orchestra errors, commit a baseline for the rest, block on new errors
